newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU probes P&O/Sea-Land/Maersk container trade deal.
newsitem.headline: EU probes P&O/Sea-Land/Maersk container trade deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was probing an agreement between P&O Nedlloyd , Sea-Land Service Inc, A.P. Moeller-Maersk Line and Orient Overseas Container Line on container trade between North America and Europe.
The accord, which was filed for EU regulatory approval in November 1996, provides for the companies to agree on tariffs and capacity as well as on inland services to shippers.

But the Commission noted that there was no obligation to adhere to any agreement and took stock of an undertaking given by the parties not to engage in inland and maritime rate making in the European Union.

The Commission said in a notice published in the EU's Official Journal of June 18, that the shipping companies controlled between 20 and 35.9 percent of the maritime transport of containerised cargo between the U.S. and north Europe in 1994.
The Commission, the EU's competition watchdog, has often taken aim at cooperation agreements in the shipping sector either in the transport of containers or passengers.

It has been trying since 1992 to force companies in the Trans-Atlantic Conference Agreement (TACA) to drop provisions on the fixing of rates on inland transport to and from ports, but despite repeated fine warnings the practice continues. The European Court of Justice has been asked to arbitrate.
All four companies involved in the so-called vessel sharing agreements are also members of TACA.
The Commission asked interested parties to comment within a month.

The Commission has also warned The Peninsular and Oriental (P&O) Steam Navigation Co and Stena Line that it is seriously concerned about their plan to pool their ferry operations on the English Channel.
There is no deadline for the Commission to rule on cooperative agreements in the shipping sector which fall under EU rules prohibiting practices which restrict trade and abuse of dominant position.
P&O and Royal Nedlloyd BV merged their container shipping interests in January. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
